title: Elixir
subtitle: A friendly functional language on the Erlang virtual machine for concurrent, fault-tolerant systems, from a first program to professional practice.
description: Elixir is a dynamic, functional programming language created by José Valim and first released in 2012. It compiles to bytecode for the BEAM, the virtual machine built for Erlang, so every Elixir program inherits Erlang's lightweight processes, message passing and the OTP framework for building systems that keep running when parts of them fail. It is used for web applications and APIs (with the Phoenix framework), real-time features such as chat, notifications and live dashboards, data pipelines, embedded devices (Nerves) and numerical computing (Nx and Livebook).

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. No functional programming background is needed. It starts with installing Elixir and running a first script, works through pattern matching, functions, collections, structs and protocols, and ends with processes, GenServers and supervisors, the gradual type system, testing, the everyday tools of the ecosystem and a complete small project.

To run the code, install Elixir (it needs Erlang/OTP, which the installers bring along) following [elixir-lang.org/install.html](https://elixir-lang.org/install.html). There is no official online playground; the community's free [Livebook](https://livebook.dev/) notebooks are the closest thing, and every program here also runs as a plain script with `elixir main.exs`. Every complete program in these lessons was run with Elixir 1.20.5 on Erlang/OTP 29 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Elixir, run scripts and explore in iex, and learn the core language: immutable values, pattern matching, functions, modules and the pipe operator.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Work with collections through Enum and Stream, model data with structs and protocols under the gradual type checker, and handle control flow, errors and tests the way Elixir teams do.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Build with processes, messages and links, structure services with GenServer and supervisors, and ship a complete project with Mix, Hex and an overview of Phoenix and LiveView.
